name: US jobless claims
summary: US jobless claims 4-week average 197k, at its 52-week low
state: Initial US jobless claims were 194,000 in the week to 24 Oct, holding the four-week average at about 197,000, level with its 52-week low and far from the 15% Watch line (Department of Labor via FRED). The next weekly figure is due on 5 Nov.
for_you: Layoffs remain low by historical standards, so the US labour market shows no sign of sudden stress.
why: Weekly claims are the earliest hard data on US layoffs; a sustained rise usually comes before the unemployment rate turns.
drivers: Layoffs, hiring freezes, federal job cuts, storms, strikes and seasonal quirks.

rubric.normal: The 4-week average of initial claims is less than 15% above its 52-week low.
